title: Asthma: overview
text: Asthma involves persistent airway inflammation. The airways can narrow in response to triggers, making breathing harder. It is a long-term condition; symptom patterns and severity differ between people. A clinician assesses symptoms and lung function to establish a diagnosis and care plan.

title: High blood pressure: overview
text: Blood pressure describes the force that circulating blood places on artery walls. The systolic number represents pressure during a heartbeat; the diastolic number represents pressure as the heart relaxes. Persistently elevated pressure can damage the heart and blood vessels. A single reading is not a complete clinical assessment.

title: Sleep apnea: overview
text: Sleep apnea involves repeated interruptions of breathing during sleep. In obstructive sleep apnea, the upper airway becomes blocked. In central sleep apnea, the brain does not send the usual signals controlling breathing. Sleep studies help clinicians evaluate the condition. Snoring alone cannot establish the diagnosis.

title: Diabetes: overview
text: Diabetes involves blood glucose remaining too high. Insulin helps glucose enter cells. In type 1 diabetes, the body makes little or no insulin. In type 2 diabetes, insulin action and production are insufficient to maintain usual glucose levels. Over time, high glucose can harm organs including the kidneys, eyes, and heart.

title: Pneumonia: overview
text: Pneumonia is a lung infection caused by organisms such as bacteria, viruses, or fungi. Infected air sacs may accumulate fluid or pus. Symptoms can include cough, fever, chills, and difficulty breathing. History, examination, and appropriate tests contribute to diagnosis; an experimental image score alone cannot diagnose it.

title: Anemia: overview
text: Anemia involves too few healthy red blood cells to adequately carry oxygen. It can cause fatigue or weakness, with several possible underlying causes. Iron deficiency is one type, but not every anemia is caused by low iron. Clinical history and laboratory testing help distinguish the cause before selecting treatment.

title: COPD: overview
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease describes lung conditions that limit airflow and make breathing difficult. Emphysema and chronic bronchitis are common components. Tobacco smoke is an important risk factor, but other exposures and inherited factors can contribute. Lung function testing is part of clinical assessment.

title: Pleural disorders: overview
text: The pleura consists of membranes around the lungs and inside the chest. A pleural effusion is extra fluid in the space between these membranes. A pneumothorax involves air in that space. These terms describe different processes; a research model score does not establish whether either is present.

title: Metformin hydrochloride tablets: US reference label
text: This US label describes metformin hydrochloride immediate-release tablets as a prescription medicine used alongside diet and exercise for glucose control in type 2 diabetes. It includes contraindications and a serious lactic-acidosis warning. This general description does not establish suitability, dosing, or instructions for an individual or a different local product.
